correctness.rationale: For any fixed set of two-labelled vertices the unique cheapest completion labels an outside vertex one exactly when it has no neighbour in that set. I independently encoded only the two-label membership bits, with 4 column symbols and 256 overlapping four-column states, charging the optimized central-column weight on each of 1024 arcs. Synchronous relaxation stabilized and all arc slacks were checked. Exactly seven of the 244 tight arcs have a tight return path; they are precisely the arcs of the period-seven word in the finding. This proves the bound for every length by telescoping, and forces any minimum of weight 8k to follow that cycle. Each starting phase gives a distinct labelled function and the optimized completion recovers the stated labels. Direct checks give eight discrepancies for each nonzero shift in one period, hence 8k overall. The argument applies at k=1 as well: the spoke and two inner offsets in the local rule are exactly the stated neighbours.
residual_risks: Exact bounded replay plus a closed-walk proof, not a formal proof-assistant certificate; no equality classification at other lengths is certified.
